cards.f: Mean of raw data and of a frequency table
cards.b: Raw: Σx ÷ n. Table: Σfx ÷ Σf (divide by total frequency, not number of classes).
The (n + 1)/2 th value of the ordered data. Give the value, not the position.
Most frequent value. May not exist, or there may be several. Can be used for qualitative data.

cards.f: Advantage and disadvantage of the mean
cards.b: Uses all the data, but is affected by extreme values (outliers).
It is not affected by extreme values, so it is best when there are outliers (e.g. house prices).
Use class midpoints: Σfx ÷ Σf. The answer is only an estimate.
Q₁ = (n + 1)/4 th, Q₂ = (n + 1)/2 th, Q₃ = 3(n + 1)/4 th value. On a cumulative frequency graph use n/4, n/2, 3n/4.
IQR = Q₃ − Q₁. Spread of the middle 50%; not affected by extreme values.
Largest − smallest value. Affected by outliers.
σ = √(Σfx² ÷ Σf − (Σfx ÷ Σf)²). For grouped data x = midpoint.
Variance = σ², the square of the standard deviation.
(n₁x̄₁ + n₂x̄₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂). Never just average the two means unless the groups are equal in size.

cards.f: How to compare two data sets
cards.b: Make two comparisons in context, with values: location (mean or median) and spread (sd or IQR). Pair mean with sd, median with IQR.

short.q: For the data 2, 5, 5, 7, 9, 12, 14, find the mean (to 3 s.f.), the median and the interquartile range. [4]
short.model: Mean = 54 ÷ 7 = 7.71. Median = 4th value = 7. Q₁ = 2nd value = 5, Q₃ = 6th value = 12, so IQR = 12 − 5 = 7.

short.q: The table shows x: 0, 1, 2, 3 with frequencies f: 5, 8, 4, 3. Calculate the mean and the standard deviation. [4]
Times: 0 < t ≤ 10 has frequency 4, 10 < t ≤ 20 has 8, 20 < t ≤ 30 has 8. Estimate the mean time and explain why it is only an estimate. [3]
short.model: Midpoints 5, 15, 25: Σfx = 20 + 120 + 200 = 340; mean = 340 ÷ 20 = 17. It is an estimate because the exact values in each class are not known.

short.q: Group A: median 45, IQR 10. Group B: median 52, IQR 18. Make two comparisons. [2]
short.model: B's median is higher (52 vs 45), so B generally scored higher. A's IQR is smaller (10 vs 18), so A's scores are more consistent.
